main_body: wooden spear rack frame with upper crossbeam (rows 25-31), three vertical spears (rows 1-24, 32-35), and lower base box (rows 36-46)
top_band: upper crossbeam has only a 1px light tan rim at row 26 above a 4px vertical front face (rows 27-30); lower base box has a 4-5px tan top band at rows 37-41
evidence: For a frame/rack, both horizontal beams and the base must show foreshortened top faces. Reading down the rack from its top at row 25, the upper horizontal beam (rows 25-31) has only a 1px light tan rim at row 26 above a 4px vertical front face (rows 27-30, with a vertical left-edge highlight down col 1), and the spear shafts simply terminate against its top outline at row 25 rather than passing through a top surface. While the lower base (rows 36-46) has a lighter band at rows 37-41 above a 4px front face (rows 42-45), a continuous dark outline at row 36 cuts straight across all three spear shafts.

style.evidence: Compared to the Beodeul prop references (cheese stall and roofed well), the candidate lacks surface texture and wood grain. Each spear shaft (rows 8-24) is two 17px-tall columns of uninterrupted flat brown, and both the upper beam (rows 27-29) and lower box (rows 38-45) are filled with ruler-straight horizontal bands of solid colour.
